No.

While a ban on all automatic facial recognition is a legitimate stance reflecting privacy and civil liberties concerns—especially with the narrow margin in your canton—Switzerland is a federal system where cantons (like Zurich) do have autonomy in public safety matters. A blanket national ban may not align with cantonal experimentation or vary widely by locality. The balance hinges on strict oversight, transparency, storage limits, and deletion protocols rather than an outright prohibition. Thus, the nuanced reality of Swiss governance suggests "no" to a blanket ban, allowing continued policy experimentation and debate rather than permanent prohibition.
